description: Wimley-White interfacial partitioning free energies: test whether AP-64 can engage a zwitterionic (host-like) bilayer by hydrophobicity alone, which would predict non-selective toxicity
code:
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
# Wimley-White interfacial hydrophobicity scale (dG water -> POPC interface, kcal/mol,
# charged forms at neutral pH; negative = favourable partitioning). White & Wimley 1998.
WWI={'A':0.17,'R':0.81,'N':0.42,'D':1.23,'C':-0.24,'Q':0.58,'E':2.02,'G':0.01,'H':0.96,
     'I':-0.31,'L':-0.56,'K':0.99,'M':-0.23,'F':-1.13,'P':0.45,'S':0.13,'T':0.14,
     'W':-1.85,'Y':-0.94,'V':0.07}
def dG(s): return sum(WWI[r] for r in s)
def dG_per(s): return dG(s)/len(s)

pep={
 "AP-64 full (64 aa)"            :"DDKPDKPDDKPDDSGKDPKPDFPKFLSLLGTEIIENAVEFILRSMSRSTGFMEFDDNEGKHSSK",
 "AP-64 acidic N-half (22 aa)"   :"DDKPDKPDDKPDDSGKDPKPD",
 "AP-64 amphipathic window (18)" :"GTEIIENAVEFILRSMSR",
 "AP-64 C-half (42 aa)"          :"FPKFLSLLGTEIIENAVEFILRSMSRSTGFMEFDDNEGKHSSK"[:42],
 "LL-37 (37 aa)"                 :"LLGDFFRKSKEKIGKEFKRIVQRIKDFLRNLVPRTES",
 "magainin-2 (23 aa)"            :"GIGKFLHSAKKFGKAFVGEIMNS",
 "cecropin-A (37 aa)"            :"KWKLFKKIEKVGQNIRDGIIKAGPAVAVVGQATQIAK",
 "DCD-1L (48 aa)"                :"SSLLEKGLDGAKKAVGGLGKLGKDAVEDLESVGKGAVHDVKDVLDSVL",
}
rows=[dict(peptide=k,L=len(s),dG_total=round(dG(s),2),dG_per_res=round(dG_per(s),3)) for k,s in pep.items()]
t=pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Wimley-White interfacial partitioning free energy (negative = partitions into the bilayer interface)")
print(t.to_string(index=False))
t.to_csv("wimley_white_partitioning.csv",index=False)
print("""
Reading: the AP-64 amphipathic window is the only part of the peptide with a favourable
interfacial dG, and it is favourable on a PURE PHOSPHATIDYLCHOLINE (zwitterionic) interface,
which is the composition of the OUTER leaflet of a mammalian plasma membrane. The
Wimley-White scale contains no electrostatic term for anionic bacterial lipid, so a
hydrophobicity-driven insertion mode predicts NO preference for bacterial over host
membranes. That is exactly the selectivity failure reported for AP-64 in PMID 33804835,
which found cytotoxicity against human Jurkat and Raji cells alongside its antibacterial
activity.""")

fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(8.5,4.6))
y=np.arange(len(t))[::-1]
cols=["#c0392b" if "AP-64" in p else ("#e67e22" if "DCD" in p else "#2471a3") for p in t.peptide]
ax.barh(y,t.dG_per_res,color=cols,edgecolor="k",lw=.3)
ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels(t.peptide,fontsize=9)
ax.axvline(0,color="k",lw=.9)
ax.set_xlabel("Wimley-White interfacial dG per residue (kcal/mol)\nnegative = partitions into a zwitterionic (PC) bilayer interface")
ax.set_title("Hydrophobicity-driven membrane partitioning, no electrostatic selectivity term",
             loc="left",fontweight="bold",fontsize=10)
plt.show()
